question.:question/problem:
Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=x^{2} - 3 x + 10$ whose tangent has a slope of $-1.$

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{2} - 3 x + 10.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{2} - 3 x + 10\right) \\
&= (1)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-3)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 2 x - 3
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=-1$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x - 3 &= -1 \\
2 x &= 2 \\
x &= 1
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $-1$ at the point where $x=1.$

$$

Let $f(x)=x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 13 x - 8.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 13 x - 8\right) \\
&= (1)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (-6)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-13)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 3 x^{2} - 12 x - 13
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=2$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
3 x^{2} - 12 x - 13 &= 2 \\
3 x^{2} - 12 x - 15 &= 0 \\
3 \left(x - 5\right) \left(x + 1\right) &= 0 \\
x &= -1,\,5
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x>0$, the required coordinate is $x=5.$

Let $f(x)=3 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 102 x - 1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(3 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 102 x - 1\right) \\
&= (3)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (-6)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-102)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 9 x^{2} - 12 x - 102
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=-6$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
9 x^{2} - 12 x - 102 &= -6 \\
9 x^{2} - 12 x - 96 &= 0 \\
3 \left(x - 4\right) \left(3 x + 8\right) &= 0 \\
x &= - \frac{8}{3},\,4
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x>0$, the required coordinate is $x=4.$

Find the **positive** $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=2 x^{3} - 15 x^{2} - 43 x - 1$ whose tangent has a slope of $-7.$

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{3} - 15 x^{2} - 43 x - 1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(2 x^{3} - 15 x^{2} - 43 x - 1\right) \\
&= (2)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (-15)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-43)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 6 x^{2} - 30 x - 43
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=-7$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
6 x^{2} - 30 x - 43 &= -7 \\
6 x^{2} - 30 x - 36 &= 0 \\
6 \left(x - 6\right) \left(x + 1\right) &= 0 \\
x &= -1,\,6
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x>0$, the required coordinate is $x=6.$

Find the **positive** $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=x^{3} + x^{2} - 15 x + 11$ whose tangent has a slope of $1.$

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{3} + x^{2} - 15 x + 11.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x^{3} + x^{2} - 15 x + 11\right) \\
&= (1)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (1)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-15)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 3 x^{2} + 2 x - 15
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=1$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
3 x^{2} + 2 x - 15 &= 1 \\
3 x^{2} + 2 x - 16 &= 0 \\
\left(x - 2\right) \left(3 x + 8\right) &= 0 \\
x &= - \frac{8}{3},\,2
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x>0$, the required coordinate is $x=2.$

Find the **positive** $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=2 x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 46 x - 10$ whose tangent has a slope of $-10.$

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 46 x - 10.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(2 x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 46 x - 10\right) \\
&= (2)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (-3)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-46)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 6 x^{2} - 6 x - 46
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=-10$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
6 x^{2} - 6 x - 46 &= -10 \\
6 x^{2} - 6 x - 36 &= 0 \\
6 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x + 2\right) &= 0 \\
x &= -2,\,3
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x>0$, the required coordinate is $x=3.$

Find the $x$-coordinates of the points on the curve $y=3 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 102 x - 1$ whose tangent has a slope of $-6.$

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=3 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 102 x - 1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(3 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 102 x - 1\right) \\
&= (3)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (-6)\cdot 2\cdot x + (-102)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 9 x^{2} - 12 x - 102
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=-6$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
9 x^{2} - 12 x - 102 &= -6 \\
9 x^{2} - 12 x - 96 &= 0 \\
3 \left(x - 4\right) \left(3 x + 8\right) &= 0 \\
x &= - \frac{8}{3},\,4
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $-6$ at the points where $x=- \frac{8}{3},\,4.$
